question: Can the existing generic ggml chunked KDA helper materially reduce the current exact-macro causal core on Lucebox4 without changing terminal logits or any committed KDA/MLA state byte?

prior.helper_origin: direct port of llama.cpp delta-net chunking already present in server/src/delta_net_chunked.cpp
prior.known_warning: The helper previously produced final-state drift in Qwen3.5; this experiment treats that as a preregistered risk, not a surprise to explain away.

protocol: Build one binary and run a same-binary M64 control/candidate/reversal on Lucebox4 gfx1151 under the single-owner GPU lease.
The only candidate switch is DFLASH_KIMI_EXPERIMENT_CHUNKED_KDA=1; the control leaves it unset.
Keep the exact-macro provider policy, prompt IDs, route/slab policy, cache sizes, and all other execution flags identical.
Capture full terminal logits and a canonical binary dump of every committed recurrent convolution state, recurrent SSM state, and populated MLA row after the state-sensitive continuation.
Require byte-identical logits and state dumps, identical output IDs, identical logical traffic, and no provider/runtime fallback before interpreting timing.
Run M1024 only after an M64 GO.

gate.go: all exactness gates pass and candidate causal-core wall is at most 50% of the matched control
gate.promising_but_incomplete: all exactness gates pass and candidate causal-core wall is below 80% but above 50% of control; retain only as a kernel-optimization lead
gate.no_go: any exactness failure, any runtime failure, or less than 20% matched causal-core reduction

scope: This is the cheapest test of the existing helper inside today's Core8-grouped executor. A negative result does not falsify a true prompt-wide DPLR/FlashKDA kernel, because this path sees eight-row groups and uses generic ggml operators. It must not be called FlashKDA or a 100 tok/s result.
